newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end broadly flat as mkt eyes strike.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end broadly flat as mkt eyes strike.

text.p: Prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange ended mixed, broadly stable Thursday in weak trade as the market nervously eyed developments in an ongoing dispute between the government, unions and business over wage rises, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index edged up 0.60 percent to 9,466.05, as 19 stocks rose, 12 fell and 14 closed flat.
A 27 percent hike in gasoline prices midnight Wednesday did not provoke violent protests, allaying some fears, but the threat of a one-day national strike remained, brokers said.
Venezuela's largest union has threatened to stage a 12-hour strike August 6 to protest the fuel price hike and to pressure private sector companies to raise wages.
"The market was fairly quiet, waiting to see what happens with the strike calls and salary rises," said Cavelba broker Rafael Alcantara.
Although troubled by the disputes, the market is taking a measured rather than panicked viewpoint, brokers said.
"If the strike is successful, foreign investors will pull out of the market because they are more easily scared by these things than locals," one said.
Volume was slim on Thursday with 1,009 trades worth a total of 4,573 billion bolivars ($9.2 million).

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas fell 0.50 bolivar to 811 bolivars, telephone company CANTV rose 10 bolivars to 3,090 bolivars. Steelmaker Sivensa edged up 0.85 bolivar to 278 bolivars even though it reported lower third-quarter net profits of $15.9 million.
Generally negative earnings reports were being shrugged off by the market on the expectation of improved results as the Venezuelan economy shows further recovery, brokers added.
